citation: Lecerf JM, Clerc E, Jaruga A, et al. Postprandial glycaemic and insulinaemic responses in adults after consumption of dairy desserts and pound cakes containing short-chain fructo-oligosaccharides used to replace sugars. Journal of Nutritional Science. 2015;4:e34.
protocol: Two studies: dairy dessert (210 g; control 218.9 kcal, 48.1 g carbohydrate, 2.2 g fat, 6.1 g protein vs reduced-sugar version) and pound cake (100 g; control 461 kcal, 58.3 g carbohydrate, 22.1 g fat, 6.4 g protein vs reduced-sugar); crossover within each study. Blood at -5, -1, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 min.
population: Healthy adults: dairy-dessert study mITT n = 24, pound-cake study mITT n = 33 (sex, age and BMI in the paper); France.

reports.where: Table 2: iAUC 0-120 and Cmax per product

note: Everyday foods with exact macronutrients, including a fat-containing cake. Insulin is in mU/l (the footnote gives the pmol conversion). Use the control products. Only in figures: time courses (Fig. 2). Meal kinds: mixed meal.
